rows.notes: The study is labelled 'Review' and is a descriptive overview of the Czech Republic's climate-change challenges and the CzechGlobe research infrastructure (ICOS, ACTRIS, ANAEE, InterSucho, etc.). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or model runs on soil moisture monitoring or drought-tolerant crops; the only figures are a GDP composition chart (Eurostat), a site map, an NEP comparison attributed to unpublished data of other authors, and a biomass map adapted from Brovkina et al. 2016. Nothing in the text evaluates whether soil moisture monitoring (sensors) makes farming more resilient to rainfall variability; InterSucho is only described as providing drought guidance for irrigation, with no result reported. Q1 is therefore 'no' and all other questions 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete, though pages 2, 7, 11 and 13 contain duplicated/overlapping text from an OCR artefact of the peer-review draft overlay. The paper is an institutional review/perspective piece rather than a primary study.
